entities.text: Right to Fair  Compensation and Transparency in Land  Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement  Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel has also brought to the  notice of this Court that I.A.No.5 of 2025 has  been filed, in view of the subsequent  developments.

He submits that the writ appeal  itself would become infructuous in view of the  fact that the acquisition proceedings are taken  up at a fast pace and there is every possibility  of Award being passed in the nearest future.

The learned Advocate General  appearing for the respondents would submit that the process of acquisition would become final after an Award is passed in respect of the land in question and that a counter-affidavit would be filed by the respondents at the earliest and the issue of adequacy of material handed over to the appellants can always be gone into at that stage.

Sri K.S.Murthy, learned senior counsel would also submit that the question of validity of the notification under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 as well as the validity of the consideration of the objections of the appellants, by the District Collector have also been raised in the present appeal and the same would become a bar to the appellants for moving any other writ petitions.
It is clarified that the said issues are left open and the appellants are at liberty to challenge the said proceedings before the appropriate forum.
In that view of the matter, post the matter on 15.12.2025 for hearing.
Pleadings to be completed till then.
